traits: Pale-yellow outer tepals
Darker trumpet-shaped corona
Narrow grey-green leaves
daffodil.habitat: Moist meadows, woods and woodland edges in Britain.
daffodil.season: Usually March to April in Britain.
daffodil.note: Daffodil is a broad name. This folio uses the wild daffodil as its example.
culture: Wordsworth remembers golden daffodils moving in the breeze. The memory lifts his spirits when he is alone.
art: Daffodils and calla lilies mirror each other on pale paper.
Yellow trumpet-shaped flowers and white calla lilies form a symmetrical decorative pattern.

traits: Usually a single nodding flower
Three longer white outer tepals
Shorter inner tepals often marked green
snowdrop.habitat: Moist, well-drained ground in partial shade, often under deciduous trees.
snowdrop.season: Late winter to early spring in British garden records.
snowdrop.note: Snowdrop refers to several species. This page describes the common snowdrop.
culture: A flower that opens ahead of spring
Andersen's snowdrop opens while the weather is still cold. The wind and cold tease it for blooming so early.

traits: Small white bells along an arching stalk
Oval to narrowly ovate leaves wider than the stalk
Underground stems can form colonies
lily-of-the-valley.habitat: Cool, shaded places with moist, humus-rich soil.
lily-of-the-valley.note: Lily of the valley belongs to the asparagus family.
culture: May Day good luck in France
Giving lily of the valley on 1 May expresses a wish for good luck in this French tradition.

traits: Blue-violet bells often hang to one side
Tips of the tepals curl outward
Long narrow leaves emerge near ground level
bluebell.habitat: Native to western Europe. In Britain it grows in woods and along hedges and grassland.
bluebell.season: Usually April to May in Britain.
bluebell.note: This page describes the English bluebell. Spanish bluebells and their hybrids are separate taxa.
culture: Woodland Trust records stories in which hearing bells in a bluebell wood signals the presence of fairies.
Bluebells and the spines of old books
The National Trust records that a sticky substance from English bluebell bulbs was once used in bookbinding.
A guide to bluebells in the UK

traits: Narrow leaves grow from a corm
Cup-shaped flowers
The representative species comes in white and shades of purple
crocus.habitat: Well-drained open ground including lawns, where it may naturalise.
crocus.season: Mainly spring, sometimes into early summer in RHS records.
crocus.note: The genus includes autumn and spring flowerers. This folio describes the spring crocus.
culture: Cambridge traces the cultivation and uses of dried saffron stigmas. The spice comes from Crocus sativus, a relative of the spring crocus.

traits: Sword-shaped grey-green leaves
Large flowers with colours that vary by cultivar
Bearded irises often have a fuzzy strip on the outer tepals
iris.habitat: Sunny planting beds with good drainage.
iris.season: May to June in British horticultural records.
iris.note: The representative plant is a bearded iris listed by the RHS.
culture: Van Gogh painted a flowerbed of blue-violet irises, a white bloom and intersecting leaves.
In the Iliad, Iris appears as Laodice and calls Helen to watch the duel between Menelaus and Paris. The association suggests Iris as a name for a messenger.
art: Blue-violet irises fill a flowerbed, with one white bloom at left.
Van Gogh painted this garden at Saint-Rémy in 1889. The blue-violet flowers make the single white iris easy to spot.

traits: Orange tepals with dark spots
Nodding flowers with strongly recurved tepals
Dark bulbils can form in the leaf axils
tiger-lily.habitat: Often grown in sun and moist soil.
tiger-lily.note: Tiger lily can refer to several lilies. The example here is Lilium lancifolium.
culture: Alice wishes the Tiger-lily would speak and the flower immediately replies, opening a conversation with the garden.

traits: Broad lance-shaped leaves
The representative plant usually has a single layer of tepals
Colours include yellow, orange, red and purple-red
tulip.habitat: Sunny, well-drained beds for this ornamental bulb.
tulip.note: Garden tulips include several species and hybrids. Cultivated bulbs under this name may have hybrid parents.
culture: Judith Leyster painted the named tulip Vroege Brabantsson in watercolour during the Dutch tulip trade.
A black tulip and two names
Cornelius proposes naming the black tulip Rosa Barlœnsis, combining Rosa's name with his own.

traits: Nodding bell-shaped flowers
A pink and purple checkerboard pattern is common
Slender grey-green leaves
fritillary.habitat: Moist meadows, including a documented Oxford college meadow.
fritillary.note: Fritillary names several species. This folio uses the snake's-head fritillary with its checkerboard markings.
culture: Kew records a local Fritillary Sunday in Ducklington, where the plant grows in nearby meadows.

traits: A single head contains many small flowers
Usually yellow ray florets around the edge
Often darker disc florets in the centre
sunflower.habitat: Native to North America and widely grown in open, sunny gardens.
sunflower.season: Mid to late summer in North Carolina horticultural records.
sunflower.note: This page describes the familiar annual sunflower.
culture: Van Gogh used different yellows for the flowers, vase and background in the Amsterdam version.
The sunflower measures the sun's steps
Blake's sunflower counts the steps of the sun and yearns for the golden end of its journey.
art: Two cut sunflower heads lie at different angles against a blue ground.
This Paris still life shows two cut sunflowers, with the seed heads and curling petals filling much of the frame.

traits: White rays around a yellow centre
Ray tips sometimes blush pink
Low rosette of spoon-shaped leaves
daisy.habitat: Lawns and short turf in Britain. It tolerates regular mowing.
daisy.season: Can flower through much of the year in Britain.
daisy.note: Daisy is a broad name. This folio describes the common daisy.
culture: Robert Burns starts with a small daisy crushed during ploughing and connects the accidental damage to human fortunes.

traits: Yellow flower heads appear before the conspicuous leaves
Short, scaly flower stalks
Broad, toothed leaves and underground rhizomes
coltsfoot.habitat: Open disturbed ground and gardens, where the rhizomes spread.
coltsfoot.note: The scaly stalk and flowers appearing before the leaves help distinguish coltsfoot from a dandelion.
culture: The Met records old names likening the leaf to a horse's foot. The English name preserves the association.

traits: Flower heads made up of yellow ray florets
Often deeply lobed leaves in a basal rosette
Ripe seed head forms a white puffball
dandelion.habitat: Lawns, flower beds and cracks in paving in Britain.
dandelion.season: Flowers over a long season and is especially common in spring.
dandelion.note: Dandelions include many closely related forms. The RHS representative profile supplies the scientific name here.
culture: In Bradbury's novel, dandelion wine preserves something of summer and becomes a way to write about childhood and the seasons.

traits: Wrinkled leaves in a basal rosette
Nodding yellow flowers clustered at the top of a thin stem
Tubular flowers often marked orange at the mouth
cowslip.habitat: Grassland, woodland edges and hedgerows in Britain, often on calcareous soil.
cowslip.season: Usually April to May in Britain.
cowslip.note: Cowslip can resemble its relative the primrose and their hybrids.
culture: Ariel's bed in the flower bell
Ariel sings about lying in a cowslip's bell in The Tempest. The tiny flower gives the audience a sense of the spirit's scale.

traits: Glossy yellow petals in a shallow cup
Upright, hairy growth
Palmately divided leaves
buttercup.habitat: Meadows and other grassy ground, including moist, moderately drained soils.
buttercup.season: Early to midsummer in British horticultural records.
buttercup.note: Buttercup includes several species. The representative plant here is meadow buttercup.
culture: A yellow reflection under the chin
Newell records a children's game in which a yellow reflection from a buttercup supposedly indicates a fondness for butter.

traits: Often a single white star-shaped flower, sometimes tinted pink
Petal-like sepals
Deeply divided leaves that can carpet woodland
windflower.habitat: Deciduous woods, where it flowers before the tree canopy closes.
windflower.season: Usually March to May in Britain.
windflower.note: This folio uses wood anemone. The name Anemone nemorosa is also used for it.
culture: Adonis and the flower in the wind
Venus brings a flower forth from Adonis's blood in Ovid. An English translation calls it an anemone and describes the wind carrying its petals away.

traits: Overlapping rounded petals
Many cultivars have dark blotches near the centre
Wide variation in colour and pattern
pansy.habitat: A cool-season plant for beds and containers in sun or partial shade.
pansy.season: Depends on variety and sowing time. Some garden varieties flower from autumn into spring.
pansy.note: This profile describes a modern garden hybrid. Historical pansies may refer to older forms or relatives.
culture: Ophelia links pansies with thoughts when distributing flowers in Hamlet. The association comes from this scene.

traits: Evergreen shrub or small tree with alternate, glossy, finely toothed leaves
Often solitary flowers in white, pink, red or variegated colours
Single flowers expose their stamens. Cultivars can be densely double.
camellia.habitat: Native to parts of eastern China, Korea, Japan and Taiwan. Often grown in partial shade with moist, well-drained soil.
camellia.season: Usually late winter to early spring, with regional and cultivar variation.
camellia.note: Gardeners may use camellia for several species. This page describes Camellia japonica.
camellia.comparison: Compare bloom time and leaf and flower size with sasanqua camellia. Sasanquas usually flower from late autumn into winter and have smaller flowers. The seasons overlap, so use several clues together.
culture: The bouquet in the theatre box
Marguerite brings opera glasses, sweets and camellias to the theatre. Her florist starts calling her the Lady of the Camellias.
Su Shi's camellias in the snow
Su Shi visits the temple alone and ends with flame-red flowers against snow. The image belongs to the poem, while flowering dates vary by garden.
art: Red-and-white striped camellias open along a leafy branch.
Look for the red streaks on the petals, the glossy leaves and the unopened bud in Kazumasa Ogawa's print.

traits: Deciduous shrub with opposite, toothed leaves
Round mopheads or flatter lacecaps with larger outer flowers
Large, petal-like parts are usually the sepals of sterile flowers
hydrangea.habitat: Native to Japan according to Kew. In gardens it is often found in partial shade and moist, well-drained soil.
hydrangea.season: Usually summer. Flora of China records June to August for the typical variety.
hydrangea.note: This folio describes bigleaf hydrangea. Similar common names can also refer to unrelated shrubs with rounded flower clusters.
culture: The blue hydrangea in Flora Japonica
Plate 52 shows a blue flower head under the name Hydrangea Otaksa. The Kyoto catalogue and Kew connect that historical name to bigleaf hydrangea.
Philipp Franz von Siebold and Joseph Gerhard Zuccarini
art: A blue hydrangea flower head sits above broad green leaves on an illustration from Flora Japonica.
The plate is captioned Hydrangea Otaksa. Courtesy of the Graduate School of Science, Kyoto University. The image was resized and converted to WebP.
Philipp Franz von Siebold and Joseph Gerhard Zuccarini (authors)
Graduate School of Science, Kyoto University

traits: Deciduous small tree that often flowers on bare branches
Fragrant flowers can be white or pink
Ovate, toothed leaves appear after the flowers
plum-blossom.habitat: Native from south-central China to northern Indochina, including open woods, stream sides and slopes.
plum-blossom.season: Often late winter to early spring.
plum-blossom.note: Wintersweet belongs to a different family, although it also has fragrant winter flowers.
culture: Shadows and fragrance in the garden
Lin Bu places the shadow of the plum branches above shallow water and its fragrance in the dusk.
Little Plum Trees in the Hill Garden
Green and smoked mume fruit in Chinese food history
The Palace Museum records mume fruit being used to add acidity. Historical accounts describe salting and drying green fruit for baimei and smoking riper fruit for wumei.
art: A curving ink branch hangs down, with pale blossoms on its smaller twigs.
Wang Mian painted plum branches on silk. The Met associates winter-flowering plum with endurance in the Yuan period.

traits: Deciduous tree, often with pink flowers
Single flowers typically have five petals
Narrow, toothed leaves
peach-blossom.habitat: Kew treats peach as a cultivated plant originating in north-central China. Orchards generally provide sun and drainage.
peach-blossom.season: Usually spring, with fruit ripening in summer.
peach-blossom.note: Ornamental peach cultivars vary in flower colour and can have double flowers.
culture: Tao Yuanming's fisherman follows a stream through blossoming peach trees to the entrance of a secluded village.
art: A section of a handscroll shows green cliffs, a winding stream, fields and houses.
Zhang Hong retells Peach Blossom Spring in a handscroll. The museum page shows the work from right to left.

traits: Round leaves with stalks attached near the centre
Flowers are held above the water and have a prominent central receptacle
The receptacle develops into the familiar lotus seed head
lotus.habitat: A perennial of calm, sunny, shallow water, with rhizomes anchored in mud.
lotus.note: This is the sacred lotus, a member of the lotus family.
lotus.comparison: Look for an unbroken, round lotus leaf with a stalk near the centre. Common water lilies usually have floating leaves with a notch toward the centre. A lotus seed head is another useful clue.
culture: Zhou Dunyi describes how the lotus rises out of mud, then uses its upright bearing as an image of moral character.
Yang Wanli moves from distant green lotus leaves to pink-red flowers bright in the summer sun.
Leaving Jingci Temple at Dawn to See Off Lin Zifang
Lotus leaves and birds in ink
Compare the ink washes and birds in this handscroll with the coloured pair of lotus paintings.
art: A pair of silk hanging scrolls with pink lotus flowers, green leaves and waterbirds.
Look for buds and open flowers. On the museum's page you can zoom in on fallen petals, older leaves and ripening seed heads.

traits: Evergreen shrub or small tree with opposite leaves
Tiny fragrant flowers cluster in the leaf axils
Cultivars come in white, pale yellow and orange
osmanthus.habitat: Native from the Himalayas into parts of East Asia and Indochina. Often grown in sun or partial shade with good drainage.
osmanthus.season: Often autumn. Some forms or climates also produce spring flowers.
osmanthus.note: Here the common name refers to sweet osmanthus. The single character gui can have other meanings in historical texts.
culture: Li Qingzhao praises the flower's quiet colour and persistent fragrance, comparing it with plum and chrysanthemum.
Partridge Sky · Pale Yellow and Gentle
Scenting tea and sweets with osmanthus
The Wellcome catalogue for an eighteenth-century print records the use of male osmanthus blossoms to scent tea and confectionery. The print uses the historical name Olea fragrans.
art: An old print of an osmanthus branch with paired leaves, tiny flower clusters and enlarged flower parts.
Miller illustrates the branch and enlarged flower parts separately. Olea fragrans is a historic name that Kew lists as a synonym.

traits: Deciduous shrub with persistent woody stems
Divided leaves and large flowers at branch tips
Cultivars vary widely in colour and petal count
tree-peony.habitat: Kew accepts this representative name as a hybrid. Woody peonies are often grown with good drainage and sun or light shade.
tree-peony.note: The multiplication sign in the scientific name indicates a hybrid. Garden tree peonies include several groups.
culture: The flower that stirs the capital
Liu Yuxi contrasts the flowers in a courtyard and pond with the tree peony that draws the city out when it blooms.
art: White, pink and scarlet peonies bloom among leaves on a hanging scroll.
This Edo-period painting originally formed part of a folding screen and was later mounted as a hanging scroll.

traits: A deciduous woody vine that twines around supports
Pinnate leaves and drooping clusters of blue-violet pea flowers
Long, velvety pods after flowering
wisteria.habitat: Native to China. In cultivation it grows in sun to partial shade and well-drained ground.
wisteria.season: Spring, often before the leaves have fully opened.
wisteria.note: This page represents Chinese wisteria. Japanese wisteria and other relatives can also have drooping flower clusters.
culture: Li Bai starts with vines climbing into a tree, then describes birds hidden in leaves and scent carried on the wind.
art: Blue-violet and pale flower clusters hang among green leaves in a woodblock print.
Kamisaka Sekka uses blocks of violet and green to describe the cascading flower clusters.
